title: Massachusetts Schedule II and III single-fill quantity framework
subtopic: Schedule II and III quantity limits
rule_summary: Massachusetts generally limits Schedule II and III opioid prescriptions to a 30-day supply and recognizes defined 90-day pathways for OUD drugs, non-opioid Schedule II or III drugs, and implantable infusion pumps.
exam_relevance: The pharmacist must classify the drug and indication before selecting the 30-day or qualifying 90-day pathway, and must separately check more restrictive rules such as the first-opioid limit.

authority.name: Board Policy 2024-05
authority.section: Schedules II and III Quantity Limits

numeric_facts.conditions: Schedule II or III opioid without a more restrictive controlling rule
OUD drug, non-opioid Schedule II or III drug, or implantable infusion pump meeting the policy

exceptions: A more restrictive statute, including an applicable first-opioid limit, remains controlling.
common_confusions: The 90-day pathway is not a universal Schedule II or III allowance.
The framework does not directly set the single-fill maximum for a Schedule IV drug.
verification_notes: Current Massachusetts statute and Policy 2024-05 checked on 2026-08-13.
